name: capital-stack-news-gdelt-go-api
description: Go port of capital-stack-news-gdelt-api (GDELT news aggregator: fetch worker + SQLite cache + read API /news/articles /timeline /tone /topics), shadow stage: runs next to the Node container on its own port and its own cache, outside every request path (ticket #1882)

native_build._doc: Same multi-stage template as c3bot-relay-go (#1873): compiled in golang on the arch-matched runner (oci-apps is arm64), shipped as one static binary on distroless static nonroot.

parity-compare._doc: Reference = the Node service (user-news_capital-stack-news-gdelt-api/src/code/server.ts under node 22 with better-sqlite3) and the Go port, both fed by one fake GDELT upstream; 26 requests (limit clamps, on-demand fetch, total and partial upstream failure, 404 envelope, OPTIONS, POST) must give identical status, CORS headers and raw bodies.

parity-mutation.cmd: o=$(mktemp); PARITY_MUTATE=1 PARITY_REQUIRE=1 go test -count=1 -timeout 8m -tags parity -run TestParity ./parity/ >"$o" 2>&1; grep -q 'requests differ' "$o"
parity-mutation._doc: Mutation proof: the Go port is fed a skewed upstream; the harness must report differing requests (the grep passes only then, not on a build error).

_doc_shadow: Shadow stage (#1882). The live Node news-gdelt (container capital-stack-news-gdelt-api, port 3019, volume news-gdelt_news_gdelt_cache) is untouched. This container has no env_file and no secret, caches on its own tmpfs and binds the oci-apps WG IP only. Two quirks of the Node service are reproduced on purpose for parity and listed for a follow-up: the freshness check reads row.fetchedAt (the column is fetched_at) so every on-demand request refetches upstream, and /news/topics therefore omits lastFetch for cached topics. Switch-over (Caddy route, mesh name) is a separate step after the live comparison.
